e-means clustering

Source: R/emeans.R
emeans.Rd

Mini-batch k-means with exponential-moving-average centroid updates (Bessa et al., 2026, arXiv:2611.09501). Batch size and step size come from fitted scaling laws, so the only inputs are the data, k, and the epoch budget. In a few epochs it typically reaches a lower within-cluster sum of squares than 25 Lloyd iterations.

Usage

emeans(
  x,
  k,
  nepochs = 5,
  batch_law = c("auto", "throughput", "quality"),
  batch_size = NULL,
  alpha0 = NULL,
  spherical = FALSE,
  unused_threshold = NULL,
  max_points_per_centroid = NULL,
  precision = c("double", "single"),
  final_assign = TRUE,
  seed = 1234L,
  n_threads = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

x

Numeric matrix or data frame, one row per point.

k

Number of clusters, or a k x d matrix of initial centers.

nepochs

Epoch budget; fractions allowed (e.g. 1.5).

batch_law

"auto" (quality law when d <= 16, else throughput), "throughput", or "quality" (batch about 8 times smaller).

batch_size, alpha0

Optional overrides. Giving batch_size alone keeps the step law for alpha0.

spherical

Cluster unit vectors by cosine similarity. Rows of x must already be unit-norm; centers are returned as unit vectors.

unused_threshold

Revival threshold tau: clusters with mass below tau * mean(mass) are revived. NULL gives 0.1, or 0 (off) when d <= 2.

max_points_per_centroid

If set and nrow(x) > max_points_per_centroid * k, train on a random subset of that many rows (as faiss.Kmeans).

precision

"double", or "single" to store the training data and compute distances in float32 (about 2x faster, half the memory). Batch statistics, centroids and masses always accumulate in double precision, and withinss is computed from the original data. As in the faiss FP32 path, single precision assigns poorly when the data sit far from the origin (the error grows with the squared norm of the rows); centre the data first, e.g. with scale(x, scale = FALSE). Double precision hits the same limit at offsets around 1e8.

final_assign

If TRUE (default), assign every row of x to the final centers, so cluster, withinss and size describe the returned centers (as stats::kmeans()). If FALSE, cluster holds labels from the last training pass, and rows left out by max_points_per_centroid are NA.

seed

Integer seed for initialization, shuffling and revival. Does not touch R's random number generator.

n_threads

Threads for assignment. Defaults to getOption("emeansR.threads"), else physical cores minus one (at most two when the _R_CHECK_LIMIT_CORES_ environment variable is set).

verbose

Print the recipe and per-epoch objective.

Value

An object of class c("emeans", "kmeans") with components cluster, centers, totss, withinss, tot.withinss, betweenss, size, iter (epochs), ifault (0), plus obj (moving-pass objective per epoch), iteration_stats, recipe, n_splits, spherical and precision.

Details

Each epoch visits the rows in a fresh random order in batches of batch_size. Every batch is assigned to the nearest centroids, and each touched centroid moves towards its batch mean with weight alpha * n_j / N_j, where the mass N_j is itself an exponential moving average and alpha follows a cosine schedule from alpha0 to alpha0 / 10. Every five updates, clusters with mass below unused_threshold * mean(mass) are revived by splitting large clusters (picked with probability proportional to mass). The returned centers are the exact means of the points assigned during the last epoch.

Examples

set.seed(1)
x <- rbind(matrix(rnorm(2000, 0), ncol = 2), matrix(rnorm(2000, 5), ncol = 2))
fit <- emeans(x, k = 2, nepochs = 3, n_threads = 1)
fit$centers
#>            [,1]        [,2]
#> [1,] -0.0150379 -0.01895623
#> [2,]  5.0136701  5.01438322
table(fit$cluster)
#> 
#>    1    2 
#>  999 1001
